First listed 2026-02-27 · episode or wrap

Trump Tariff Turmoil, Private Credit Risk Grows, & AI’s Software Fears | The Weekly Wrap

Eisman treats tariff policy as disruptive but unlikely by itself to overwhelm US resilience. His main concerns are AI capital returns, software-heavy private credit and insurance links. He distinguishes payment-network moats from exposed software, remains skeptical of solar and Warner Bros valuation, and finds Netflix more interesting. Nvidia and Circle operating growth is supported, while Circle reserve interest is dominant rather than its sole revenue. Private-credit transaction ownership, insurance leverage and loss forecasts require further primary verification.

How he reasons here

  • Focus on growth, funding and related-party incentives across private credit and life insurance.
  • Use network effects to distinguish payments from software-disruption fears.
  • Separate reported earnings strength from market narrative and valuation.
  • Recognize that institutional information advantages do not guarantee outperformance.
